title: Inconsistent tenant attribution after API key rotation and sub-account mapping
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Several customers reported mismatched usage charges and rate-limit counts during and after API key rotations and when using nested sub-accounts (parent->child project mapping). Affected customers saw spikes attributed to the wrong org or missing attribution for up to 45 minutes after key rotation. This ticket tracks investigation, root cause, mitigation, and fix rollout.

Observed behavior:
- When an API key is rotated (old_key -> new_key), some requests that carry the new_key are attributed to the old org_id in billing events and rate-limit counters for ~5-45 minutes.
- Sub-accounts with parent mapping sometimes show tokens billed to parent org instead of the child workspace when requests are proxied through the routing layer during autoscaling.
- Rate-limit enforcement sometimes blocks requests for the wrong quota bucket (parent instead of child), generating 429s that don't match the customer's expected quota.

Why this matters:
- Incorrect per-tenant billing and quota enforcement leads to overcharging/undercharging, broken SLAs, and customer trust issues. High priority because multiple enterprise customers have complained and one account reported a $12k mismatch.

Reproduction steps (local):
1) Create org A with workspace child-A1 and parent billing mapping enabled.
2) Issue API key K1 for child-A1. Send steady traffic: 50 reqs/s -> verify usage recorded in billing-db:org=child-A1.
3) Rotate key: create K2 and deactivate K1. Immediately send traffic using K2.
4) Observe billing events for a subset of K2 requests show org=parent-A while dashboard shows child-A1 usage.
5) Simulate high routing churn (scale up routing pods) to reproduce faster.

Initial investigation notes:
- Attribution flow: API request -> authentication service maps api_key -> key_id -> owner mapping -> routing attaches org_id -> metering window writer persists events.
- We log a cache layer (redis) between auth service and metering writer for key->owner mapping to avoid DB hits. Cache entries are keyed by key_id and TTL is 30m.
- During rotation, key_id for new_key reuses part of the same id namespace and our cache invalidation was based on key secret rather than key id. New_key created with new key_id but the cache lookup performed a fallback by secret prefix in rare races and returned stale mapping.
- Additionally, the routing layer maintains a short-lived in-memory map for active connections; when pods restart during autoscale, there is a window where requests are forwarded through a pod that still has stale parent mapping cached and does not refresh before processing the first requests.
- Logs show mismatched owner_id in auth-service logs correlated with pod restarts and cache misses. See logs: grafana link and raw logs in logging bucket.

Impact scope:
- Preliminary query against usage events (bigquery:billing.events) for last 7 days shows ~0.6% of token events have inconsistent owner_id vs resolved_owner in request metadata. Roughly 7 customers affected with 1 enterprise high-dollar exposure.

Temporary mitigations applied (on 2026-03-11):
- Force cache bypass for key lookups when key rotation detected: auth-service now checks DB first for any key with created_at < 10m. Deployed as hotfix to staging and then canary.
- Increased logging and alerting for owner_id mismatches; created dashboard panel: grafana/redwood/billing/attr-anomalies.
- Notified impacted customers and opened billing dispute cases.

Root cause hypothesis:
1) Cache invalidation race during key rotation: cache entries are not invalidated atomically when a key is deactivated/rotated, leading to stale owner mappings returned for new secrets that share prefix or id-derived heuristics.
2) Routing pod in-memory map not stamped with latest owner mapping after autoscale/restart, and code path does not handle cache miss fallback correctly under high concurrency.

Proposed long-term fix:
- Change cache keying to strictly use immutable key_id (UUID) and never rely on secret prefix heuristics. Ensure key_id is always returned from key provisioning and used end-to-end.
- Add immediate cache invalidation hooks in key rotation workflow: on rotate/deactivate, emit invalidation event to redis pubsub and routing pods to evict mapping.
- Add fallback synchronous lookup path on owner-mismatch: if metering writer sees org_id != resolved_org in request metadata, perform a synchronous resolution and re-route or re-attribute before persisting.
- Add unit + integration tests covering rotation + autoscale scenarios.

Acceptance criteria:
- No owner_id mismatch after key rotation in end-to-end integration tests (simulated autoscale).
- Metric owner_id_mismatch_rate < 0.01% over 48h after rollout.
- Backfill and corrective billing process established for impacted customers with sign-off from finance and legal.

Runbook / Artifacts:
- Initial runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/billing-attr-rotation-runbook
- Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/billing/attr-anomalies
- BigQuery investigation query: bq://redwood.billing.events#owner_mismatch_2026_03
- Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2789 (patch: cache-key-fix + invalidation)

2026-03-11 14:05 - Rahul Singh (assignee): Completed initial logs correlation. Found 3 routing pods showing owner mismatch traces during scale-up. Pushed hotfix to staging to bypass cache for recent rotations. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2774

2026-03-12 09:30 - Mei Chen (SRE): Canary rollout of hotfix to 10% traffic. Anomaly rate fell from 0.6% -> 0.12% in canary. Observed higher DB read latency; added circuit-breaker for auth-service DB reads.

2026-03-12 17:50 - Priya Patel (PM): Coordinated customer communications. Finance requested itemized list of affected customers and estimated exposure. Legal wants a full timeline before final notification. Added billing-disputes label.

2026-03-13 16:00 - Ava Martinez: Please include a migration/backfill plan for usage events that were misattributed. Finance prefers adjusting invoices rather than issuing credits when possible. Added ENG-5750 as follow-up for backfill automation.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed to bypass Redis cache for keys created within last 10 minutes and added extra logging. Canary reduced anomaly rate from 0.6% to 0.12%. Support paused rotations for affected customers where feasible.
next_steps: 1) Merge PR #2789 and run full regression in staging (Rahul). 2) Add pubsub invalidation + end-to-end test for rotation+autoscale (estimate 8pts). 3) Run billing backfill for affected window (ENG-5750). 4) Post-mortem and customer remediation package drafted by Priya + Finance.
